title: WPF and WinForms
sub: The UI thread, Dispatcher and Task.Run
cards/0/body: A single UI thread draws the window and handles clicks. Controls may only be touched from that thread. await in a handler brings you back there on its own, which is why label.Text = ... works after await.
cards/1/task: After await, the handler writes to label.Text. Someone added ConfigureAwait(false), and everything broke. Fix it.
cards/2/q: Which exception do you get in WPF if you touch a control from another thread?
cards/2/options/0: InvalidOperationException: "The calling thread cannot access this object because a different thread owns it"
cards/2/explain: WinForms throws a similar InvalidOperationException about a cross-thread operation.
cards/3/title: Getting back to the UI thread by hand
cards/3/body: If your code is already on another thread (a timer event, a library callback), ask the UI thread to do the work:
cards/4/body: await by itself doesn't move work off the UI thread: synchronous code before the first await runs right there. Hand heavy calculations to the pool with Task.Run, and show the result after await.
cards/5/q: A button handler has await CalculateAsync(), yet the window still freezes for 3 seconds. Why?
cards/5/options/0: CalculateAsync computes synchronously until its first await, which means on the UI thread
cards/5/explain: async doesn't make code run in the background. Hand the calculation to Task.Run.
cards/6/q: Put what happens on a click in order
cards/6/items/0: The handler starts on the UI thread
cards/6/items/1: Task.Run hands the calculation to the pool
cards/6/items/2: The UI thread is free and handles clicks
cards/6/items/3: The calculation ends and the continuation is queued to the UI
cards/6/items/4: The UI thread shows the result
cards/6/explain: While the pool computes, the window stays alive.
cards/7/q: Which are true? Select all that apply.
cards/7/options/0: await in a handler returns to the UI thread
cards/7/options/1: Dispatcher.InvokeAsync runs code on the UI thread
cards/7/options/2: Task.Run moves heavy calculation off the UI thread
cards/7/options/3: A button handler must be async Task
cards/7/explain: The event sets the handler's signature, so async void is fine there.
cards/8/pairs/0/1: WPF: run on the UI thread
cards/8/pairs/1/1: WinForms: run on the UI thread
cards/8/pairs/3/1: Brings await back to the WPF UI thread
